stated: The Conservative Party will back farmers by increasing the UK-wide farming budget by £1 billion over the Parliament, introducing a legally binding target for food security, improving public sector procurement of local food, and reforming planning to fast-track farm infrastructure.

source.quote: Champion our rural communities by backing farmers with a legal target and additional investment for food security, and protecting our best agricultural land from solar farms. ...Increase the UK-wide farming budget by £1 billion over the Parliament, ensuring it rises by inflation in every year.

bearing_set.reason: Domestic farming support and a food-security target directly affect food supply and food costs, which are an explicit indicator of cost of living for ordinary households.

A £1bn increase in farming budget, depending on whether it is tied to environmental conditions (e.g. ELMS-style requirements), materially affects agricultural emissions, water quality, and biodiversity — agriculture being one of the largest contributors to all three.
A legally binding food security target and increased farming budget directly bear on national resilience to external supply shocks — 'resilience to external threats' is an O5 indicator.

A £1bn uplift in the farming budget, fast-tracked farm infrastructure, and improved public-sector procurement represent supply-side investment in agricultural productivity and rural economic opportunity — real effects on sector-level living standards and economic dynamism over the Parliament.

membership_note: The two core bearings are food costs (O2) and agricultural-sector prosperity/opportunity (O13). O6 (environment) is a plausible concern given farming's land-use and emissions footprint, but the policy is silent on environmental conditionality, making the direction of effect unresolvable without further detail — insufficient mechanism to clear the non-negligible bar. O4 (farm worker pay) is a real secondary concern but adequately covered by the O13 sector-level judgment at this stage. O12 (public finances) — the £1bn over a Parliament is ~£200m/year against total public spending, below a material fiscal threshold for O12 bearing.
